S001's simultaneous induction is valid: the h step uses hy=yh−2y; the x base uses xv=0 and hv=λv, and the step coefficient simplifies to (t+1)(λ−t). Repeated x action gives the displayed nonzero product for i≤λ; factorials and all positive integer factors are nonzero in ℂ, including the empty-product case i=0. In S002 each polynomial factor acts diagonally on every e_i. For fixed j, every other summand has a vanishing factor and the surviving scalar is ∏_{k≠j}2(k−j), nonzero in ℂ. Cancellation (equivalently applying an inverse scalar) proves independence. M003 gives spanning; BG001 justifies the expansion already requested in the text. Applying h to that expansion makes each coefficient multiply by −2(λ+1−i), which is nonzero for every i≤λ. Hence the first out-of-range y-power vanishes, and composition gives all higher vanishings. S003's divided factorial identities give the asserted generator actions (xe_0=0 also uses the direct H003 premise and e_0=v). Iteration yields the stated rising products; the displayed counting of ordered distinct lists by their underlying subsets proves the factorial ratios equal D015's binomial counts. Beyond the specified ranges, the string reaches a zero endpoint. The r=0 and λ=0 cases agree with the formulas. No unsupported substantive implication was found.
